errors.location: Opening paragraph and Introduction, claimed universal gate set
errors.description: The listed gates Z, S, T and CNOT cannot approximate arbitrary single-qubit unitaries: they preserve computational-basis states up to phases and permutations, whereas H creates superpositions.
errors.evidence: The Introduction says that “single-qubit Z, S and T gates together with two-qubit CNOT gate are sufficient to approximate any unitary operator in U(2)”. Every product of these gates maps a computational-basis input to another computational-basis state times a phase; the manuscript defines H|0⟩ = (|0⟩ + |1⟩)/√2.

errors.description: The proposed transversal implementation does not implement the claimed logical phase gate. Solving the real linear system Hv = w does not ensure the required phases on binary codeword superpositions.
errors.evidence: Eq. (6) gives P(−α) ⊗ P(α) ⊗ 1^⊗4 ⊗ P(α). In Eq. (5), logical zero contains both |0000000⟩ and |0110011⟩ (the latter from a = 0, b = c = 1). Eq. (6) multiplies these terms by 1 and e^{2iα}, respectively. At α = π/4 their relative phase changes to i, although a logical P(α) must leave |0⟩_L unchanged. This also invalidates the recursive construction relying on Eq. (4).

errors.location: Conclusions, formula fixing m for the finite gate set
errors.description: The prescribed denominator exponent remains 1 as the requested error decreases, so the resulting phase grid cannot provide arbitrarily fine approximations.
errors.evidence: The gate set is specified with “m = ⌈ϵ/ [log_2(1/ϵ) log_2 log_2(1/ϵ)···]⌉” and positive integers ℓ < 2^m. For sufficiently small positive ϵ this yields m = 1 and ℓ = 1, hence only the phase angle π/2. It cannot satisfy the earlier requirement |α − πℓ/2^m| < δ ≤ ϵ/⌈log_2(1/ϵ)⌉ for α = π/4.

errors.description: The stated gate-count bound tends to zero with the requested error and therefore cannot describe approximation of an arbitrary nonidentity gate.
errors.evidence: The Conclusions claim approximation to accuracy ϵ “using O(ϵ log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] ···) gates”. With the stated termination of the iterated-log product, this expression tends to zero as ϵ → 0. An integer gate count obeying that bound would eventually be zero, whereas the empty circuit is the identity and cannot approximate P(π/2) arbitrarily accurately.
